newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT, KDD say impact of new US telecom rule unclear.
newsitem.headline: NTT, KDD say impact of new US telecom rule unclear.

text.p: Japan's NTT and KDD, whose telecom licences in the United States have been delayed, said on Thursday it is still unclear if new U.S. measures to open up its telecoms market will help resolve the licence issue.

Asked if new telecoms market liberalisation plans of the U.S. will help to resolve the licence issue, a spokesman for Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd (KDD) said: "We simply don't know. The U.S. government has not even made it clear why KDD's licence in the U.S. has been delayed."

The U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) on Wednesday said it planned to liberalise access to U.S. telecoms markets for most foreign companies in line with World Trade Organisation (WTO) rules.

Among measures the FCC said it will be proposing is the elimination of the Effective Competitive Opportunities (ECO) test, which requires that a foreign country give equivalent access to U.S. companies before firms from that country can operate in the U.S. telecoms market.

A spokesman for Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) said: "We hope the new measures will prompt the FCC to quickly grant NTT a licence. Despite deregulatory steps, however, apparently some restrictions regarding individual licensing cases remain."
The spokesman said the U.S. Trade Representative's Office (USTR) could intervene to stop granting of business licences to NTT and KDD on trade policy concerns.

Earlier this year, U.S. regulators told NTT and KDD their applications for licences to offer international long-distance phone services had been put on hold so that the Clinton administration could review them over trade concerns.
The FCC said the USTR, the Commerce Department and State Department had told the FCC that the applications could "raise trade policy concerns".
The USTR has urged Japan to renew NTT's procurement pact and to scrap a 20 percent ceiling on foreign ownership in NTT and KDD.
